requirements.title: The push request
requirements.rationale: A caller names one branch in the path and may ask for force in the body; what the hub understands from both must not depend on the client.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access submits POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/branches/:name/push with no body, an empty body, `{}`, `{"force": false}`, `{"force": true}` or an object that has members other than `force`
criteria.action: take `force` as true only when the body is an object whose `force` member is the JSON value true, take it as false in every other listed case, and ignore the other members
criteria.contract: the push is carried out with that force value; the `force` member of the `parley.workspace.push` event shows it

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
the push operation is replaced by a stub that answers `pushed`
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over the bodies {none, empty, `{}`, `{"force":false}`, `{"force":true}`, `{"force":true,"extra":1}`, `{"extra":1}`}: call the push handler with a stubbed push operation that records the force flag it is given; assert status 200 and that the recorded flag is true for the two bodies with `force` true and false for the others

criteria.condition: the body is not empty and is not a JSON object, or its `force` member is not a JSON boolean
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over the bodies {`[]`, `"x"`, `5`, `{` (malformed), `{"force":"true"}`, `{"force":1}`, `{"force":null}`}: r = push(body); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert the stubbed push operation was not called and the event count is unchanged

criteria.condition: the `:name` path segment contains percent-encoded characters
criteria.action: percent-decode the segment exactly once and use the result as the branch name
criteria.contract: the `branch` member of the answer is the once-decoded name: `fix%2F42` gives `fix/42` and `a%2525b` gives `a%25b`

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
the hub's copy has the branches `fix/42` and `a%25b`
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, through the hub's real router, a table {path segment `fix%2F42` with hub branch `fix/42`, path segment `a%2525b` with hub branch `a%25b`}: r = POST the route; assert r.status == 200 and r.json.branch == the hub branch name; assert origin now has that branch

criteria.condition: the decoded branch name is not a valid branch name under the branch-name rule of WS-FR-011
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over the decoded names {`a..b`, `-x`, `x.lock`, `a b`, `@`, `a//b`, `.hidden`, `x/`} sent percent-encoded: assert status 400 and `error_type` `invalid_request`; assert the stubbed push operation was not called

criteria.condition: the caller is a member of the workspace's organization without write access, or authenticates with a PAT that lacks the scope `workspaces:write`, or has no access to the workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request before reading the body
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` for the member; HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope` for the PAT without the scope; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` for the caller without access; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, through the hub's real router and access rule, a table over the callers {org member with an API key, owner with a PAT holding only `workspaces:read`, a user outside the organization}, each sending the invalid body `[]`: assert 403 forbidden, 403 insufficient_scope, 404 not_found in that order; then the owner with an API key, the owner with a PAT holding `workspaces:write` and the admin token each send no body: assert 200

requirements.title: Refusals before the push
requirements.rationale: Some branches and some workspaces must never be pushed by this route; refusing them before origin is contacted keeps the refusal free of side effects.

criteria.condition: the workspace's status is not `ready`, or a reclone, archive or delete is running on it
criteria.action: refuse the request with the state guard's answer
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_busy` for `pending`, `cloning` and a running reclone, archive or delete; `workspace_not_ready` for `failed`; `workspace_archived` for `archived`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

setup: a repository workspace record put in each state through the store
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over the workspace states {pending, cloning, ready with the maintenance marker set, failed, archived}: assert status 409 and the `error_type` of the contract; assert the stubbed push operation was not called

criteria.condition: the workspace is a fork
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `fork_has_no_origin`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: with a workspace record of kind `fork` whose parent is ready, push branch `work`; assert status 400 and `error_type` `fork_has_no_origin`; assert the stubbed push operation was not called

criteria.condition: the workspace's mode is `carry_patch` and the branch is the workspace's `integration_branch`
criteria.action: refuse the request, with and without `force`
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `integration_branch`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over force {false, true}: with a carry-patch workspace whose `integration_branch` is `deploy`, push `deploy`; assert status 403 and `error_type` `integration_branch`; and with a standard workspace that has a branch `deploy`, assert the push of `deploy` is not refused

criteria.condition: the workspace's mode is `carry_patch` and the branch is the branch of a registered patch that is not deleted
criteria.action: refuse the request, with and without `force`
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `patch_branch`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over force {false, true}: with a carry-patch workspace and a patch-branch lookup that reports `patch/a` as registered and `patch/gone` as not registered, push `patch/a`; assert status 403 and `error_type` `patch_branch`; assert the push of `patch/gone` is not refused; and with no lookup registered assert the push of `patch/a` is not refused

criteria.condition: the workspace's mode is `carry_patch` and the patch-branch lookup returns an error
criteria.action: refuse the request and push nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 503 with `error_type` `unavailable`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: with a carry-patch workspace and a patch-branch lookup that returns an error, push `feature`; assert status 503 and `error_type` `unavailable`; assert the stubbed push operation was not called

criteria.condition: `force` is true and at least one of the workspace's protected-branch globs matches the whole branch name, where `*` matches any run of characters except `/`, `**` matches any run of characters including `/` and every other character matches itself
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `protected_branch`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

setup: the workspace's stored setting `protected_branches` holds the row's globs, on a settings registry filled by RegisterSettingKeys of package 11; for the last row the workspace has no stored `protected_branches` value
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table of (globs, branch, protected?) with force true: ([`main`], `main`, yes); ([`main`], `main2`, no); ([`main`], `x/main`, no); ([`release/*`], `release/1.x`, yes); ([`release/*`], `release/1/x`, no); ([`release/**`], `release/1/x`, yes); ([`**`], `a/b/c`, yes); ([`*`], `a/b`, no); ([], `main`, no); (globs not set, the default branch, yes): assert status 403 and `error_type` `protected_branch` exactly for the rows marked yes, and that the stubbed push operation is called for the others

criteria.condition: the hub's copy of the repository has no branch `refs/heads/<name>`
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `branch_not_found`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: with a real copy that has no branch `nope`, push `nope` with force false; assert status 404 and `error_type` `branch_not_found`; assert origin received no connection (the test origin's request counter is unchanged)

criteria.action: for any request that fails more than one check, answer with the failure of the first check in this order: body, branch name, workspace status, fork, integration branch or patch branch, forced push of a protected branch, branch exists
criteria.contract: the answer is that of the earliest failing check

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table of requests that each fail two adjacent checks: (body `[]` and name `a..b`) gives 400 invalid_request for the body; (name `a..b` on an archived workspace) gives 400 invalid_request; (archived carry-patch workspace, integration branch) gives 409 workspace_archived; (failed status on a record of kind fork) gives 409 workspace_not_ready; (carry-patch workspace, force true, integration branch that also matches a protected glob) gives 403 integration_branch; (force true, protected glob matches, branch missing) gives 403 protected_branch; (force false, branch missing) gives 404 branch_not_found

requirements.title: Fast-forward push
requirements.rationale: Without force a push may only add commits to origin's branch, so it can never discard work the hub has not seen.

criteria.condition: a request passes every check, `force` is false, and origin has no such branch or origin's branch is an ancestor of the hub's
criteria.action: read the head of `refs/heads/<name>` once, push that commit to the same branch on origin and answer the result `pushed`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {branch: the branch name, sha: the 40-character id of the pushed commit, remote: "origin", remote_url: the workspace's git_url without userinfo, result: string} with result `pushed`; origin's branch is at `sha`

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
commits are added to the hub's copy with `git` on disk
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, with the real push operation, a table {hub branch `feature` that origin lacks; hub `feature` two commits ahead of origin's `feature`; the protected default branch `main` one commit ahead of origin's}: r = push(branch, no body); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json == {branch, sha: hub head, remote: 'origin', remote_url: the test origin's URL, result: 'pushed'}; assert the test origin's branch head == r.json.sha

criteria.condition: a request passes every check and origin's branch is already at the hub's head of that branch, with `force` false or true
criteria.action: change nothing on origin and answer the result `up_to_date`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {branch: the branch name, sha: the 40-character id of the pushed commit, remote: "origin", remote_url: the workspace's git_url without userinfo, result: string} with result `up_to_date`; origin's branch is unchanged

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over force {false, true} on the unprotected branch `feature` whose head equals origin's: assert status 200 and result `up_to_date`; assert origin's branch head is unchanged; and with force true and no recorded origin head for the branch, assert the same answer

criteria.condition: `force` is false and origin's branch is not an ancestor of the hub's, because the two diverged or origin's branch is strictly ahead
criteria.action: leave origin's branch as it is and refuse the push
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `non_fast_forward`; the message names the recorded origin head of the branch when one is recorded and says to sync or to push with force; origin's branch and the recorded origin head are unchanged

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
the test origin's branch is moved with `git` on disk after the clone
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table {origin's `feature` has a commit the hub lacks and the hub has one origin lacks; the hub's `feature` is one commit behind origin's}: r = push('feature'); assert r.status == 409 and `error_type` `non_fast_forward`; assert the message contains the recorded origin head, the word `sync` and the word `force`; assert origin's branch head and the recorded origin head are unchanged

criteria.action: for any push, send exactly the one ref `refs/heads/<name>` to origin and no other branch and no tag

check.pseudocode: in internal/gitrepo/push_test.go: with a hub copy holding the branches `a` and `b` and the tag `v1` that origin lacks, run the push operation for `a`; assert origin has `refs/heads/a`; assert origin has neither `refs/heads/b` nor `refs/tags/v1`

criteria.condition: the branch is protected and `force` is false
criteria.action: push it fast-forward only, as any other branch
criteria.contract: the answers of a non-forced push; never `protected_branch`

criteria.action: for any push, authenticate to origin with the workspace's origin credential as resolved from the workspace's secrets at the time of that push
criteria.contract: origin receives HTTP Basic authentication with user `x-token-auth` and the token when `GIT_PAT` is set, else with `GIT_USERNAME` and `GIT_PASSWORD` when both are set, else none; a secret changed between two pushes is used by the second

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, with a test origin that requires Basic authentication, a table {`GIT_PAT` = t1 with origin accepting x-token-auth:t1; `GIT_USERNAME` = u and `GIT_PASSWORD` = p with origin accepting u:p}: assert the push answers 200; then make origin accept only x-token-auth:t2, store `GIT_PAT` = t2 as the workspace secret and push a new commit; assert 200 without restarting the hub; assert the credential appears neither in the copy's git configuration nor in the arguments of the `git` process

requirements.title: Forced push with a lease
requirements.rationale: A rewritten branch must be publishable, but never at the price of commits that reached origin after the hub last looked.

criteria.condition: `force` is true, origin's branch is at the origin head the hub last recorded for it, and that commit is not an ancestor of the hub's head
criteria.action: replace origin's branch with the hub's head and answer the result `forced`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {branch: the branch name, sha: the 40-character id of the pushed commit, remote: "origin", remote_url: the workspace's git_url without userinfo, result: string} with result `forced`; origin's branch is at `sha`

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: rewrite the hub's unprotected `feature` so that its head is not a descendant of origin's head, with the recorded origin head equal to origin's head; r = push('feature', {force: true}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.result == 'forced'; assert origin's branch head == r.json.sha

criteria.condition: `force` is true and the push is a fast-forward of origin's branch from the recorded origin head, or creates a branch for which no origin head is recorded and which origin does not have
criteria.action: push the hub's head and answer the result `pushed`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {branch: the branch name, sha: the 40-character id of the pushed commit, remote: "origin", remote_url: the workspace's git_url without userinfo, result: string} with result `pushed`; origin's branch is at `sha`

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table with force true {hub `feature` one commit ahead of origin's and of the recorded origin head; hub branch `new` that origin lacks and that has no recorded origin head}: assert status 200 and result `pushed`; assert origin's branch head == sha

criteria.condition: `force` is true and origin's branch is neither at the hub's head nor in the state the lease names: it moved since the hub last saw it, it exists although the hub never recorded an origin head for it, or it was deleted although the hub recorded one
criteria.action: overwrite nothing on origin and refuse the push
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `origin_moved`; origin's branch (or its absence) and the recorded origin head are unchanged

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
origin is changed with `git` on disk after the clone; recorded origin heads are set or removed with SetOriginHead and DeleteOriginHead of internal/gitrepo on the hub's copy
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table with force true on a rewritten hub `feature` {origin's `feature` got a new commit after the last recorded head; no origin head is recorded and origin has `feature` at another commit; an origin head is recorded and origin's `feature` was deleted}: r = push; assert r.status == 409 and `error_type` `origin_moved`; assert origin's ref state and the recorded origin head are exactly as before the call

criteria.action: for any forced push, state the expected value of origin's branch explicitly as the lease and never send a force that origin would apply whatever its branch holds

requirements.title: Failures of the push itself
requirements.rationale: A caller can act on a failed push only when the answer says which of origin, the credential, the network or the clock stopped it.

criteria.condition: origin refuses the update of the branch itself, for example by a branch rule or a server-side hook
criteria.action: report origin's refusal with origin's reason
criteria.contract: HTTP 422 with `error_type` `origin_rejected`; the message carries origin's reason; origin's branch and the recorded origin head are unchanged

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: with a test origin whose hook refuses every update with the text `branch is locked`, push a fast-forward of `feature`; assert status 422 and `error_type` `origin_rejected`; assert the message contains `branch is locked`; assert origin's branch head and the recorded origin head are unchanged

criteria.condition: origin asks for authentication and the workspace has no origin credential, or origin rejects the stored credential
criteria.action: report that origin could not authenticate the hub and say which of the two cases applies
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with `error_type` `origin_unauthenticated`; the message says either that the workspace has no credential or that origin rejected the stored credential; origin's branch and the recorded origin head are unchanged

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over the test origin's behaviour after the clone, each pushing a fast-forward of `feature`: (requires Basic authentication, workspace without credential) gives 502 origin_unauthenticated with a message containing `no credential`; (requires Basic authentication, stored `GIT_PAT` not accepted) gives 502 origin_unauthenticated with a message containing `rejected`; (answers HTTP 403 to the push) gives 502 origin_forbidden; (answers HTTP 404) gives 502 origin_not_found; (listener closed) gives 502 origin_unreachable; (serves a certificate the hub does not trust) gives 502 origin_unreachable; (answers HTTP 500) gives 502 upstream_error; for every row assert the recorded origin head is unchanged

criteria.condition: origin answers that the credential may not push to the repository
criteria.action: report the refusal
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with `error_type` `origin_forbidden`; origin's branch and the recorded origin head are unchanged

criteria.condition: origin has no repository at the workspace's `git_url`, or the credential cannot see it
criteria.action: report that the repository was not found
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with `error_type` `origin_not_found`; origin's branch and the recorded origin head are unchanged

criteria.condition: origin cannot be reached because name resolution, the connection or TLS fails
criteria.action: report that origin is unreachable
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with `error_type` `origin_unreachable`; origin's branch and the recorded origin head are unchanged

criteria.condition: the push fails in any way not named by another criterion of this requirement or by `non_fast_forward` and `origin_moved`
criteria.action: report an upstream failure
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with `error_type` `upstream_error`; origin's branch and the recorded origin head are unchanged

criteria.condition: the push has not finished when its deadline of 2 minutes passes
criteria.action: end the `git` process and report a timeout
criteria.contract: HTTP 504 with `error_type` `origin_timeout`, answered no later than 5 seconds after the deadline; no `git` process of the push remains; the recorded origin head is unchanged

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: build the handler with a push deadline of 300 ms and a test origin that stalls after accepting the connection; t0 = now; r = push('feature'); assert r.status == 504 and `error_type` `origin_timeout`; assert now - t0 < 5.3 s; assert the push operation's child process has exited; assert the recorded origin head is unchanged

criteria.condition: the origin credential cannot be read from the workspace's secrets
criteria.action: fail the request without contacting origin and without falling back to an anonymous push
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with `error_type` `internal`; origin is not contacted, no branch and no recorded origin head changes, and no event is written

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: with a credential resolver that returns an error, push `feature`; assert status 500 and `error_type` `internal`; assert the stubbed push operation was not called and the event count is unchanged

requirements.title: Records after a push
requirements.rationale: The hub's memory of origin and the audit record must both reflect every push that reached origin, whoever was still listening.

criteria.condition: a push ends with the result `pushed`, `forced` or `up_to_date`
criteria.action: record the pushed commit as the origin head of that branch, by setting the ref refs/remotes/origin/<name> of the hub's copy, and write the workspace's origin_head_sha for the default branch in the same store transaction as the push event
criteria.contract: the ref refs/remotes/origin/<name> of the hub's copy, which is the recorded origin head of the branch, resolves to `sha`; for the default branch the workspace's `origin_head_sha` equals `sha`

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table {fast-forward of the default branch `main` (pushed); forced push of `feature` (forced); `feature` already on origin with no recorded origin head (up_to_date)}: after the 200, assert gitrepo's OriginHead of the branch in the hub's copy == r.json.sha; for `main` assert the workspace record's `origin_head_sha` == r.json.sha

criteria.action: for any push that fails, leave the recorded origin head of the branch as it was before the call

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, a table over the failures {non_fast_forward, origin_moved, origin_rejected, origin_timeout} produced as in the checks of those answers: read refs/remotes/origin/<name> of the hub's copy before and after the call (absent counts as a value); assert they are equal

criteria.condition: a push handed to origin succeeds
criteria.action: write exactly one `parley.workspace.push` event
criteria.contract: one event of type `parley.workspace.push` with `workspace` the slug, the caller as actor, `resource_type` `branch`, `resource_id` the branch name and metadata {branch, sha, force, ok, remote_url} with ok true and `result` equal to the answer's result, and no `error_type`

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, with the real event log, a table over the results {pushed, forced, up_to_date}: n = count(events of type parley.workspace.push); push; assert the count is n + 1; assert the new event's workspace, actor, resource_type == 'branch', resource_id == branch and metadata == {branch, sha, force, ok: true, remote_url, result} with the values of the answer and the request's force

criteria.condition: a push handed to origin fails with `non_fast_forward`, `origin_moved`, `origin_rejected`, `origin_unauthenticated`, `origin_forbidden`, `origin_not_found`, `origin_unreachable`, `upstream_error` or `origin_timeout`
criteria.action: write exactly one `parley.workspace.push` event
criteria.contract: one event of type `parley.workspace.push` with `workspace` the slug, the caller as actor, `resource_type` `branch`, `resource_id` the branch name and metadata {branch, sha, force, ok, remote_url} with ok false and `error_type` equal to the answer's `error_type`, and no `result`; `sha` is the hub's head that was offered

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, with the real event log, a table over the nine failures produced as in the checks of those answers: n = count(push events); push; assert the count is n + 1; assert the new event's metadata.ok == false, metadata.error_type == r.json.error.error_type, metadata.sha == the hub's branch head and that metadata has no member `result`

criteria.condition: a request is refused before the push: by access, body, branch name, workspace status, fork, integration branch, patch branch, protected branch, a missing branch or an unreadable credential
criteria.action: write no event
criteria.contract: the event log holds no new `parley.workspace.push` event after the refusal

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go, with the real event log, a table with one request per refusal named in the condition: n = count(push events); send the request; assert the answer is the refusal; assert count(push events) == n

criteria.condition: the caller disconnects while the push is running
criteria.action: let the push run to completion or to its deadline and then write the origin head and the event as for a connected caller
criteria.contract: origin's branch is at the pushed commit, the recorded origin head equals it and one `parley.workspace.push` event with ok true exists, although no response was delivered

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: with a test origin that delays its answer by 500 ms, start the push over a real connection and cancel the client's request after 100 ms; poll up to 5 s; assert origin's `feature` == the hub head; assert the recorded origin head == the hub head; assert exactly one new push event with ok true; then repeat with an origin that stalls and a handler deadline of 300 ms and assert exactly one new event with ok false and error_type `origin_timeout`

criteria.condition: origin accepted the push and the transaction that writes origin_head_sha and the event cannot be committed to the store
criteria.action: report a hub failure, put the ref refs/remotes/origin/<name> back to the value it had before the call, and leave origin as it is
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with `error_type` `internal`; the recorded origin head is unchanged and no event is written

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/push_test.go: with a stubbed push operation that answers `pushed` and a store whose transaction fails, push `feature`; assert status 500 and `error_type` `internal`; assert refs/remotes/origin/feature of the hub's copy has the value it had before the call (absent when it was absent), origin_head_sha is unchanged and the event count is unchanged

requirements.title: Scrubbed messages
requirements.rationale: Origin's own error text can repeat the URL it was called with; nothing the hub passes on may carry the credential.

criteria.action: for any error message this route returns and any text it writes into an event, replace every occurrence of the origin credential's value by `[redacted]` and remove the userinfo from every URL
criteria.contract: neither the token nor the password of the workspace's origin credential occurs in the response or in the event; `https://user:pass@host/path` reads `https://host/path`

setup: a ready repository workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that accepts pushes, with the caller as its owner

requirements.title: The `parley workspace push` command
requirements.rationale: Publishing a branch is a one-line step in a developer's or an agent's script.

criteria.condition: a user runs `parley workspace push <slug> <branch>` without `--force`
criteria.action: send POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/branches/<branch>/push with the slug and the branch each percent-encoded as one path segment and the body `{"force": false}`, and print the hub's answer
criteria.contract: exit status 0; stdout is the push answer as one JSON document; stderr is empty

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/workspace_test.go: against an httptest server that records the request and answers 200 with a push answer, run `workspace push demo fix/42`; assert the request's method is POST, its escaped path is `/api/v1/workspaces/demo/branches/fix%2F42/push` and its body decodes to {force: false}; assert exit 0, stdout decodes to the answer and stderr is empty

criteria.condition: a user runs the command with `--force`
criteria.action: write a warning on stderr that origin's branch may be replaced, then send the request with the body `{"force": true}` and print the hub's answer
criteria.contract: exit status 0; stdout is the push answer alone; stderr holds the warning, written before the request is sent

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/workspace_test.go: against an httptest server whose handler records what the command's stderr holds at the moment the request arrives, run `workspace push demo main --force`; assert the body decodes to {force: true}; assert the stderr captured at request time already contains `may be replaced`; assert stdout decodes to the answer and nothing else

criteria.condition: the hub answers the push with an error
criteria.action: print the hub's error envelope on stderr as received
criteria.contract: exit status 1; stdout is empty; stderr holds the envelope with the hub's `error_type`

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/workspace_test.go, a table over hub answers {409 non_fast_forward, 409 origin_moved, 403 protected_branch, 504 origin_timeout}: run the command; assert exit 1; assert stdout is empty; assert stderr decodes to an envelope whose code and error_type are the hub's

criteria.condition: the command is given fewer or more than two arguments
criteria.action: report a usage error and send nothing
criteria.contract: exit status 2; stderr holds an envelope with `error_type` `usage_error`; the hub receives no request

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/workspace_test.go, a table over the argument lists {none, `demo`, `demo main extra`}: run the command against an httptest server; assert exit 2 and `error_type` `usage_error` on stderr; assert the server received no request

criteria.action: give the push request a timeout of 3 minutes in place of the client's default of 30 seconds
criteria.contract: an answer the hub gives after more than 30 seconds and less than 3 minutes is printed; a request still unanswered after 3 minutes ends with `client_error` and exit status 2

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/workspace_test.go: run the command with an HTTP transport stub that records the deadline of the request's context and answers at once; assert the deadline lies between 179 s and 181 s after the start of the command

execution_paths.title: A developer publishes a landed branch from the shell

steps.action: runs `parley workspace push demo main` after the hub's `main` has moved ahead of origin's
sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/branches/main/push with the body {"force": false} and a 3-minute timeout
authenticates the caller, checks write access, the body, the branch name, the workspace status and the refusals, and reads the head of `main`
resolves the origin credential from the workspace's secrets and pushes that commit to `refs/heads/main` on origin, fast-forward only
authenticates the hub and fast-forwards its `main`
records the commit as the origin head of `main`, writes the `parley.workspace.push` event and answers 200 with result `pushed`
prints the answer on stdout and exits 0

real_components: parleyd HTTP server with authentication and the workspace access rule
test origin served by git http-backend over TLS
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a secrets key
a test origin that requires Basic authentication and accepts pushes
the workspace `demo` created through POST /workspaces with `git_pat` and waited for until `ready`
one commit added to the hub's `main` with `git` on disk in the hub's copy
end_state: the command exits 0 and its stdout decodes to an answer with result `pushed` and the hub's head as `sha`
the test origin's `main` is at that commit
the event log holds exactly one `parley.workspace.push` event for `demo`, with ok true

execution_paths.title: An agent's forced push is stopped by the lease and succeeds after a sync

steps.action: rewrites the branch `feature` in the hub and submits POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/branches/feature/push with {"force": true}, after another commit reached origin's `feature`
passes the checks and offers the hub's head to origin with the lease of the origin head it last recorded
finds its `feature` at another commit than the lease names and leaves it untouched
writes a `parley.workspace.push` event with ok false and error_type `origin_moved` and answers 409 `origin_moved`
submits POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/sync, which records origin's new head, and repeats the forced push
pushes with the new lease, records the origin head, writes the event and answers 200 with result `forced`
replaces its `feature` with the pushed commit

real_components: parleyd HTTP server with authentication and the workspace access rule
test origin served by git http-backend over TLS
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0
the workspace `demo` cloned from a test origin that has the unprotected branch `feature`
the hub's `feature` rewritten with `git` on disk so that it does not descend from origin's
one more commit added to the test origin's `feature` after the clone
end_state: the first push answered 409 `origin_moved` and the test origin's `feature` still held the commit added there
the second push answered 200 with result `forced` and the test origin's `feature` is at the hub's head
the event log holds two `parley.workspace.push` events for `feature`: ok false with error_type `origin_moved`, then ok true with result `forced`
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/workspace_push_test.go: r1 = post(push('demo', 'feature'), {force: true}); assert r1.status == 409 and r1.json.error.error_type == 'origin_moved'; assert origin.head('feature') == originCommit; post('/workspaces/demo/sync'); r2 = post(push('demo', 'feature'), {force: true}); assert r2.status == 200 and r2.json.result == 'forced'; assert origin.head('feature') == r2.json.sha; ev = events(type='parley.workspace.push', workspace='demo'); assert [e.metadata.ok for e in ev] == [false, true]
